newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet crude market quietly digests Brent gains.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet crude market quietly digests Brent gains.

text.p: North Sea wet Brent crude markets were quiet on Tuesday as the market digested huge gains in outright Brent levels on Monday.
"I've seen nothing on the physical front. Refiners are digesting the rally and recalculating their margins which must have lost more than 60 cents," a trader said.
June Brent trimmed part of Monday's 77 cent rally in morning trade, trading 12 cents down at $19.60 a barrel on the IPE screen at 1214 GMT.
Brent CFDs made early gains but softened towards midday with as buyers retreated.
The remainder of the week was offered at July +10 cents and next week at July +7 cents. May 27-30 sold at July flat.
Intermonth spreads held on to gains made in the U.S. aftermarket, when June/July traded at a high of +20 cents. July/August was talked at +8/+11 cents.
Three Brent dates loading May 28-30 were set to be nominated from the paper chains on Tuesday.

Traders remained relaxed about the blockade of the Sullom Voe Brent Brent export terminal by local fishermen although the protest prevented a loaded tanker from leaving the port on schedule on Tuesday morning.
Police arrived at the port late in the morning to break up the blockade.
"I don't see it being a prolonged thing," one trader said.
None of the June loading programmes for North Sea crudes had been released by midday on Tuesday, traders said.
After Tuesday's strong Brent rally, the Brent/Dubai spread continued to firm on Tuesday, with an August spread traded at +$1.36.
Dubai intermonth spreads were pegged at +20/+25 for Jul/Aug and +15/+18 for Aug/Sep.
